transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

This symptom usually indicates a blocked vent or lint filter causing overheating, which triggers the safety thermostat to cut power until it cools down. Please check that the exhaust hose is not kinked and clean the lint filter before every use. From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked airflow making it overheat and cut out. A blocked filter makes the dryer overheat, and it then cuts out to protect itself. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening (heat-pump models often have a second filter at the bottom). Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
i clean the filter regularly so its clean. cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho. no burning smell

From what you have described, the most likely cause is clear the air path / vent hose (and condenser on condensers). Check the vent hose out of the back: it should be short, without kinks or squashed sections, and clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
just pushed the dryer back further recently and the hose is crushed behind it, theres fluff in the folds of it too. is that the problem?

Yes, a crushed vent hose with fluff buildup restricts airflow and causes overheating, which triggers the safety cut-out. You need to replace or straighten the hose to resolve this issue. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
